description: A team of students and technology enthusiasts working together on NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are focused on building an innovative solution for the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge, combining software development, design, research, and problem-solving.
summary: Noqta is MoonByte’s interactive lunar landing-site exploration prototype for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It focuses on Shackleton Crater and helps users explore how terrain, sunlight, Earth visibility and rover access affect a candidate site. The 3D experience offers orbit, rover-follow, rover-camera and top-down views, illustrative terrain layers, selectable landmarks, and manual or automated rover driving. A companion data console connects to NASA GSFC PGDA Product 78 for a LOLA elevation GeoTIFF and to NASA/JPL Horizons for Sun and Earth ephemerides. NASA Moon Trek and LROC Quickmap informed our exploration of lunar imagery and topography. The current 3D terrain and environmental layers are illustrative and are not yet driven by the live LOLA raster or Diviner data. Noqta makes complex lunar site questions easier to explore and sets a clear path toward verified, date-aware site comparison.
details:
Noqta is MoonByte’s interactive prototype for exploring lunar landing-site conditions, with a focus on Shackleton Crater and the lunar south pole. It responds to the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge by making terrain and local horizon questions easier to inspect through a browser.

Users can orbit the 3D scene, follow the rover, switch to rover-camera or top-down views, and select candidate landmarks such as a connecting ridge, a permanently shadowed region, or a crater field. The terrain inspector displays modeled coordinates, elevation, slope and estimated temperature. Users can drive manually by clicking a destination or use an automated ridge route. Visual modes show illustrative thermal, slope, and shadow/ice layers.

A companion data console connects the project to NASA/JPL Horizons, requesting hourly Sun and Earth ephemeris rows for a lunar observer location and selected time window. Its DEM endpoint fetches the Site01 LOLA 5 m/pixel surface GeoTIFF from NASA GSFC PGDA Product 78, then reads raster metadata, samples, summary statistics and a SHA-256 digest. NASA Moon Trek and Arizona State University’s LROC Quickmap served as interactive references for lunar terrain, imagery and topography. The Canadian Space Agency’s Moon Exploration portal informed our broader mission context.

The 3D simulator and data console are separate: the current 3D terrain and environmental layers are illustrative, not measurements from the live LOLA raster or Diviner products. This distinction keeps the project’s data provenance clear. Planned work includes connecting verified elevation and dated Sun/Earth geometry to the 3D scene, then comparing candidate sites and mission windows.

We built the project with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js r128 and OrbitControls for WebGL, Node.js serverless functions, and the geotiff JavaScript package. It runs in a modern browser and requires no specialized hardware
and we've used the slides on a web page path for easy animation and controller
